dispatchAnchorNote: The first dispatch of this cycle carried the literal placeholder 'replace-after-hash' in place of the expected prompt digest, and was superseded mid-turn by a corrected dispatch supplying 72e7c9e3… and 0c4ba241…. I had already measured the prompt three times under the placeholder dispatch and got 72e7c9e3…, which is the value the corrected dispatch then named. That is independent evidence the prompt did not move between the two dispatches, so the anchor chain is intact despite the initial placeholder.
verdictBasis: The correction this entry makes is right, and its forensic account is exactly right — I reproduced every claim in it from git and from live bytes. The single SHOULD-FIX is that the operative clause misstates how many places need editing: it directs replacing three COORD recitals where exactly one exists.

shouldFixRecorded.location: Decision clause 1 — 'Replace the three COORD recitals of the Codex digest `a4495d16…`'
shouldFixRecorded.finding: There is one such recital in COORD, not three. Counting occurrences rather than matching lines, the false digest a4495d161df088a442a167befe7df10c8422a070d460d91016878c78b094c77d appears exactly once in the whole register, at line 2800 inside D-069's status paragraph. D-069, D-071 and D-072 are recorded as three separate entries, but only D-069 carries a verdict recital with digests; D-071 and D-072 each read 'Same turn-1 verdicts as D-069.' and contain zero 64-hex tokens between them.
shouldFixRecorded.whyItMatters: This is the operative clause of a register-mutating entry, and it is the instruction an executor follows. Someone directed to replace three recitals and finding one has to decide what went wrong: conclude the register was tampered with, stop, or — the outcome that actually damages the record — make the count true by expanding D-071 and D-072 from cross-reference form into explicit digest recitals. That would be a register-content change this entry neither authorizes nor had reviewed, performed under the belief it was completing an authorized correction.
shouldFixRecorded.distinctionDrawn: The Fact section's wording is defensible where clause 1's is not. 'The COORD entries cite Codex … as a4495d16…' is fair, because three entries are affected — D-071 and D-072 incorporate D-069's verdicts by reference, so the false digest reaches all three. But a recital is a textual site, and there is one. Clause 1 conflates entries-affected with sites-to-edit.
shouldFixRecorded.whyNotMustFix: The intended correction is unambiguous from the rest of the entry. Clause 4 states the general rule — 'Later citations of the Codex verdict must use 503d02a2…' — and the Fact section identifies the single wrong value precisely. An executor who edits the recital wherever it occurs produces exactly the right register. The entry is imprecisely scoped, not wrong about what to correct.
shouldFixRecorded.fix: Clause 1: 'Replace the single COORD recital of the Codex digest a4495d16… — in D-069's status paragraph; D-071 and D-072 inherit it by their "Same turn-1 verdicts as D-069" cross-reference and need no edit.'

summary: Subject and prompt held at their dispatched digests, both read-only. The forensic core of this entry is impeccable and I reproduced all of it independently rather than accepting the account: the live Codex verdict measures 503d02a2…, the blob committed in 5f6b4e07 measures the same, and a sha256 sweep of every committed version of that file across all refs shows exactly one version ever committed — with a4495d16… appearing in none of them. That corroborates the stated cause, an uncommitted pre-commit working-tree snapshot, precisely. My own verdict digest is unchanged at c6a6e234… and matches live bytes, so the attack axis about Claude 2's digest being rewritten alongside fails. My objection is confined to the operative clause's count: it says three recitals; there is one.
objections: C2-D073-SF1 — clause 1 directs replacing three COORD recitals where exactly one exists.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 0c4ba2413193435538386aed437fe7d5dea0eb9009613c43868ccc79bd59872b, three measurements at start and again at end, equal to the corrected dispatch's expected value and to the prompt's. Prompt held at 72e7c9e3c12e4e1908d0db3d854ac71d53e3cf54c1860c8c364ee58dffa02509. Both -r--r--r-- at both ends.

The attack 'cited live Codex digest is not 503d02a2…' fails. I hashed the file without opening it: docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-069-071-072.review-adversarial.codex.json measures 503d02a28ec575b3c038e8e259c01d470601dcf2e7a4a26ee628c048450921e1, exactly as cited, and its permissions are -r--r--r--, matching the entry's claim that the live file is frozen 0444 at that digest.

The attack 'committed HEAD blob is not that digest' fails, tested by extracting the committed content rather than trusting the assertion. git show 5f6b4e07…:<path> piped to sha256 returns 503d02a2…, so the object committed in the adoption commit is the digest the correction installs.

The stated cause is corroborated forensically. I enumerated every commit that ever touched that path across all refs and hashed the file's contents at each: exactly one committed version exists, at 5f6b4e07, measuring 503d02a2…. The false digest a4495d16… matches no committed version anywhere in history, which is precisely what an uncommitted pre-commit working-tree snapshot would look like. The entry's account — coordinator hashed a snapshot, Codex revised before git add — is consistent with the evidence and I could find no alternative explanation that fits it.

The attack 'Claude 2 digest is also being rewritten' fails, and this is the one pin I can verify absolutely because I wrote the file. My verdict measures c6a6e234ddbb15557d03a2b7d0f6f70ec1efc5e905d310b0f339b70d7109c95c, exactly the value the entry cites as unchanged, and exactly the value COORD already recites for it. Clause 1 touches only the Codex pin.
The false digest is genuinely in the register and the correct one is not yet: a4495d16… occurs once in COORD and 503d02a2… occurs zero times, so the correction is needed rather than already applied.

The attacks 'reopens or overturns D-069 / D-071 / D-072' and 'silent SATISFIED' fail. The header refuses to reopen any of the three, clause 2 states they 'remain ADOPTED. This entry does not re-decide Route B. It does not owner-record. It does not write a disposition', clause 3 refuses SATISFIED, the readiness effect is 'Zero. Adoption standing unchanged', and reversibility states 'Does not overturn D-069, D-071, or D-072.' I confirmed all three remain ADOPTED in COORD.

The attacks 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' and 'file 08 edited' fail: the header and clause 3 both refuse to authorize docs/v2/implementation/ and to edit file 08, file 08 measures unchanged at its cited digest 9495c70f…, and git reports zero modified tracked files.

The remaining cited inputs match live bytes: COORD 2af51835… and file 08 9495c70f…, and the adoption commit 5f6b4e07bb9293041e494ab08d74942878a5af97 resolves to 'D-069/D-071/D-072: select Route B for DR-006/007/009'.

The reversibility clause is unusually candid and correct for a correction entry: 'Total. Overturn: C-D073, which restores the false a4495d16… recital.' It names what an overturn would put back rather than describing the reversal abstractly.

The alternatives section rejects the two wrong ways to handle this — 'Silent COORD rewrite without review. Rejected: D-000' and 'Re-open D-069/071/072. Rejected: merits and standing unchanged' — and states the reason the third is not an option: 'cited digest ≠ live/committed bytes'.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of this subject. Not read; the file is confirmed absent at review time.

The contents of the Codex verdict on D-069/071/072. Hashed at 503d02a2… without opening. The entry's claim that the verdict word and counts are unchanged between the uncommitted snapshot and the committed file — 'CONSENT, 0 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX, 0 NOTE, per-entry CONSENT' — is therefore not something I verified. It is worth noting that this claim is unverifiable by anyone now: the a4495d16… version was never committed and exists in no ref, so unless the coordinator retained that snapshot outside git, no comparison of the two versions can be made. Nothing turns on it for the correction itself, which only makes the register point at the bytes that exist.
Whether the adoption of D-069/D-071/D-072 was sound. I reviewed that cycle and consented; this entry does not reopen it and I did not re-audit it.
The internal contents of my own D-069-071-072 verdict beyond confirming its digest is unchanged.

Whether any citation of a4495d16… exists outside COORD. I counted occurrences in the register, which is what clause 1 addresses; I did not sweep the whole corpus, though clause 4's general rule would cover any such site.

objectNote: I OBJECT with zero MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX. The entry is right about the thing that matters and its forensics are better than most: I reproduced the committed-blob hash, swept every committed version of that file across all refs, and confirmed the false digest matches nothing in history — exactly the signature of the uncommitted snapshot the entry says caused it. My own digest is untouched, which is the axis I could test absolutely. What I cannot consent to is an operative clause that tells an executor to edit three sites when one exists, because the most likely way to reconcile that instruction with the register is to expand D-071 and D-072 into explicit recitals — a register-content change nobody authorized or reviewed. The cross-reference form those two entries use is good design and should survive this correction untouched; the clause just needs to say so.
